chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the man who rejects the perfume. He said: 'It is not befitting that he rejects the prestige (or honor/gift).'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on rejecting a gift of perfume in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that rejecting a gift of perfume is discouraged not merely as a social faux pas, but because it constitutes a rejection of the giver's *karamah* (prestige or honor). This highlights the Shia emphasis on preserving social harmony and respecting the dignity of others through gracious acceptance, even of small gifts. The ruling underscores the principle that *karamah* is a tangible social asset that should not be lightly dismissed.
